items.title: Reagent and solvent inventory
paragraphs: Bismuth citrate (3.17 mmol) is suspended in oleylamine (4.2 mL); sulfur solution contains sulfur (15.6 mmol) in oleylamine (10.4 mL). Oleylamine is technical grade 70%. Bismuth citrate formulation and sulfur allotrope are unspecified. Toluene quenches/redisperses; acetone precipitates. Workup solvent volumes are unreported.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 9059), Experimental Section, Synthesis of Bi2S3 Nanowires

facts.label: Oleylamine
facts.value: 4.2 mL initial + 10.4 mL in sulfur solution; technical grade 70%.

items.title: Bi2S3 nanowire growth
paragraphs: 3.17 mmol bismuth citrate in 4.2 mL oleylamine; 100 °C under vacuum for 30 min; switch to N2 and hold 160 °C for 30 min; decrease to 130 °C and inject 15.6 mmol sulfur in 10.4 mL oleylamine through septum. Source then says “increased to 100 °C” and growth for 15–45 min. Preserve the apparent 130-to-100 °C sequence conflict. Quench with toluene; acetone-precipitate and centrifuge; remove supernatant; redisperse in toluene. Repeat precipitation/redispersion twice overall and remove most acetone.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2 (printed p. 9059), Experimental Section, Synthesis of Bi2S3 Nanowires

canonical_links.relation: general procedure; no time-resolved sample assignment

facts.label: Growth interval
facts.value: 15–45 min; not split into individually characterized datasets.

facts.label: Temperature wording
facts.value: 100 °C vacuum 30 min → N2 160 °C 30 min → decrease to 130 °C → inject → source says “increased to 100 °C”.

notes: No injection/stirring rate, centrifuge settings, yield, flask size, or workup solvent amounts.
The paper says the synthesis had been reported elsewhere and reproduces a brief method; antecedent method not checked.

items.title: Core structure and morphology
paragraphs: The authors interpret EXAFS/XANES/XPS/NMR as a bismuthinite-like Bi2S3 core. Table 1 gives nanowire Bi coordination 4.0 ± 0.2 and average first-shell distance 2.667 ± 0.003 Å; bulk comparator is 3.0 and 2.682 Å. Main text reports diameter 1.6 nm by TEM, citing SI Fig. S8; that SI image was unavailable/unverified. Figure 8 is a bulk reference; Figures 9–10 are proposed wire/surface models, not specimen-refined coordinates.

facts.label: Diameter
facts.value: 1.6 nm by TEM; SI Fig. S8 unverified.

facts.label: Phase
facts.value: Consistent with bismuthinite; no sample CIF/refinement.

items.title: Oleylamine coordination and exchange
paragraphs: Table 2 reports N/Bi = 4.4 by NMR/UV–vis and 4.3 by XPS; nearby narrative gives XPS N/Bi = 4.2. Keep both XPS values separate. S/Bi = 2.5 by XPS versus bulk 1.5; authors caution residual sulfur/polysulfide makes exact composition difficult. N 1s around 399 eV is broad and not unequivocally deconvoluted. Oleylamine exchange remains fast on the NMR time scale down to −60 °C.

facts.label: Exchange
facts.value: Fast; not slowed to coalescence at −60 °C.

items.title: Why complementary spectroscopy?
paragraphs: The authors motivate combined local-structure and ligand-sensitive measurements because the 1–2 nm cluster–nanocrystal transition and beam-sensitive wires challenge conventional diffraction/HRTEM. XAS/XPS probes core/local species; solution NMR probes ligand binding and exchange.

items.title: Why a chain-based nanowire cross-section?
paragraphs: The authors use bismuthinite’s anisotropic structure: stronger short Bi–S intrachain bonds along c and weaker interchain contacts; two proposed wire cross-sections preserve the former while cleaving along the latter. Bond-valence analysis favors the more homogeneous eight-chain model.
notes: Not specimen-refined coordinates; model omits strain, compression and surface reconstruction.

items.title: Why propose Bi–N coordination?
paragraphs: The measured first-shell Bi coordination exceeds the bulk reference value. The authors propose dative oleylamine coordination to accessible surface Bi sites; up to 75% are accessible in their preferred model. NMR/XPS show excess amine and fast exchange. Ligand occupancy is a proposed model rather than an atomic surface measurement.

evidence.locator: Main PDF pp. 8–11 (9065–9068), Figs. 9–10 discussion and conclusion

items.title: NMR acquisition and concentration method
items.text: The main article reports 1H and 13C spectra on a 400 MHz Varian Mercury at 25 °C, referenced to the proteo-solvent impurity. For concentration determination, a known amount of CH2Br2 was dissolved in 750 µL of nanowire dispersion in d8-toluene; the 1H spectrum used a 45 s interscan delay to allow full T1 relaxation. The numerical CH2Br2 amount is not stated. Variable-temperature spectra used a Varian NMR System 400 in d8-toluene from −60 to 55 °C and were also referenced to the proteo-solvent impurity. These are characterization conditions, not synthesis setpoints or an individually identified nanowire batch.
